data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan, having raised $80M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 total peers (3 public, 8 private) in the nuclear energy sector at same and adjacent stages, including Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, and public names trading under OKLO, NNE, and SMR.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using $80M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, implies $160M. Peer-median analysis across the 3-company comparable set—spanning Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A)—yields a median valuation of $808M, with a full range of $200M to $6.0B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneous stage and business maturity within the nuclear energy private market.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $136M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $484M. Key uncertainties stem from the sparse and stage-heterogeneous peer set; the 30x spread between peer minimum and maximum reflects fundamental differences in technical maturity and capital intensity within frontier nuclear subsectors. Stage alignment with direct comparables remains a material constraint on precision.
